: Judgment :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 01 / 2011-12 dated 10.03.2020 pertaining to Sy. No.38/1A measuring 1089 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 bearing Sy. No.38/1A measuring 1089 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village, have been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No. 2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.2000 (E) dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No. 1923(E) dated 13.11.2007.

The SLAO passed the award A.P. No.163/2022 on 10.04.2008 by fixing compensation amount of Rs.225/- per Square feet and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.2,71,690/- in respect of 1089 Square feet and the said amount has been deposited in favour of respondent No.1.
Subsequently, on 15.06.2011 the respondent No.1 has filed an application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.3,000/- per Square feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
A.P. No.163/2022 :GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is bad in law, in conflict with public policy of India and patently illegal.
The award suffers from Wednesbury unreasonableness.
Further the respondent No. 2 ought to have followed Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
The impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 is ex facie erroneous.
The claim made by the respondent No.1 before respondent No.2 is barred by limitation.
The impugned Arbitral Award is against the well settled law of fixation of compensation.
The Pubic Exchequer should not be put to undue burden by excess valuation.
It is the statutory duty of the Court to maintain the balance between diverse interests.
Among other grounds, prayed for the relief claimed in the petition.
.5. The respondent No. 1 and 2 though served with the notice, the respondent No.1 not chosen to A.P. No.163/2022 appear before this Court to resist the petition and r e s p o n d e n t N o .

sentences.text: The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No.1 under Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to condone the delay of 29 days in filing the petition.
.7. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the impugned award passed on 10.03.2020.
The certified copy of of the said award received by the petitioner as on 05.01.2022.

Further stated that during pandemic there was a change in the post for Project Director and the post remained vacant for several months and the petitioner has succeeded the post of Project Director of the petitioner.
Further stated that in the month of February and March 2022 several employees of the petitioner tested positive for Covid-19 and the office was completely non-functional.
Even as of today, to curb the A.P. No.163/2022 infection, the employees work on shift basis at half strength.

Further stated that due to the aforesaid reasons, the concerned department of their office could not co-ordinate with their legal counsel to pass instructions and further relevant records to challenge the order passed by respondent No.2.
Among other grounds prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.

.8. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.9.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative A.P. No.163/2022 Point No.3 : As per final order,
for the following:
REASONS .10. POINT No. 1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.11. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. K.R.
Balasubramaniam is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.38/1A measuring 1089 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification A.P. No.163/2022 dated 13.11.2007
, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO National Highways Authority Of India ... vs Balasubramaniam K R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172666193/
3 determined the compensation at Rs.225/- per Square feet for the acquired land.

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.2,71,690/- was deposited in favour of respondent No.1 as compensation.

.12. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Sri. K.R. Balasubramaniam filed an application on 15.06.2011 before the respondent No.2 claiming that the compensation fixed by the SLAO is less than the market value and hence, to enhance compensation as per NH Act 1956.

As per Circular of the Department of Registration and Stamps bearing No.CVC/BUD/5/2006- 07, Bengaluru dated 17.04.2007, the compensation amount fixed for agricultural land is Rs. 150 lakhs per acre or Rs.344/- per Square feet and the Arbitrator has added 60% on Rs.344/-, it comes to Rs.550/- (Rs.344/- + Rs.206/-).
The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.550/- by adding of 75% on Rs. 550/- per Square feet i.e., Rs. 412 + Rs. 550 = 962/-.

The SLAO fixed 250/- per Square feet for agricultural land and arrived at Rs.712/- per Square feet ( Rs. 962 - 250 = 712/- per Square feet).
.13.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No.2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance A.P. No.163/2022 value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on 22.11.2006.
As such, the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 19.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 5 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.14. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority A.P. No.163/2022 Act.

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.

However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received National Highways Authority Of India ... vs Balasubramaniam K R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172666193/
4 from the Arbitrator.

sentences.text:
In the case on hand, the Arbitrator relied on subsequent notification bearing No.
CVC/BUD/5/2006- 07 dated 17.04.2007, the said notification not produced.

The LAO enhanced the compensation to the extent of 75% claiming that the acquired land is the commercial property but there is no material on record or in the records received from the Arbitrator discloses that there is special instructions or guidelines to the Arbitrator or to the officers who are determining the A.P.
No.163/2022 market value had add the 75% to the compensation if the acquired land is commercial land.

In the award it is simply stated that 75% has been added to the compensation as the land is commercial land but there is no supporting documents to show that 75% to be added to the compensation if the land is commercial.

It is relevant to note that this 75% added after adding 60%
as per the CVC guideline value prescribed for commercial property.
Therefore the Arbitrator in total added 135% to the compensation but there is no material on record to substantiate the said enhancement.

Further it is also relevant to note that as per the CVC guidelines the additional 60%
can be added to the compensation if the land is commercial but there is no material on record to show that after adding 60% to the compensation the Arbitrator can add another 75% again on the land which has been already considered as commercial land and 60% added to the compensation.

Therefore, the Arbitrator in this case added 60% and 75% to the compensation only on the A.P.
No.163/2022 ground that the land is commercial which cannot be accepted.
.16. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.1 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the SLAO.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.17. Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.

ORDER I.A. No. 1 filed by the petitioner under Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996 to condone the delay in filing the petition is hereby allowed.
A.P. No.163/2022 Petition filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 01 / 2011-12 dated 10.03.2020 pertaining to Sy.
No.38/1A measuring1089 Sq. feet of Chikkabidrakallu village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
